SECTION CHECK   Test yourself
SC315-1  A manager responsible for costs only runs a:
A.	revenue center
B.	profit center
C.	cost center
D.	investment center
SC315-2  What distinguishes an investment center from a profit center?
A.	Its manager also answers for the assets used
B.	It earns more profit
C.	It has no costs
D.	It reports to head office
Answers and explanations are at the end of the chapter.
The manager sets prices and controls costs, but not investment
The manager controls costs only; another unit decides output
The manager controls selling effort but not production costs
The manager decides on new plant and working capital
The manager controls nothing but is charged a share of head office
No center: the charge is not controllable

EXAM TRAP   Authority first, label second
Calling a unit a profit center does not give its manager control over prices. If the question says that another unit sets the price or the volume, the center is a cost center however the company labels it.

EXAM TRAP   Contribution margin deducts only variable costs
Deducting any fixed cost before the contribution margin gives a figure that no longer measures what an extra unit adds. The cost-volume-profit work of Book 2 then no longer applies to it.

EXAM TRAP   Never close a segment on the allocated figure
A segment with a positive segment margin is covering its own costs and contributing to common costs. Closing it does not remove those common costs; they are simply shared among fewer segments.
